Senator Bailey, Representative Mathieson, and fellow members of the Health Coverage,
Insurance and Financial Services Committee, I am Representative Anne-Marie Mastraccio of House District 142, which is part of the City of Sanford and the Village of Springvale. I am here
today to introduce LD 448, An Act Regarding the Establishment of Fees and Fee Caps for
Dental Provider Licensing and Permits.

LD 448 was "submitted as a bill by the Department of Professional and Financial
Regulation, Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation (OPOR) to restore fee cap levels for the Board of Dental Practice and to make clear that the director of
OPOR has the authority to set via the rulemaking process the fees necessary to
support the board's operational needs in meeting its statutory mandates.

The department will provide the committee with more detail about this technical bill as part of their testimony. I will try to answer any questions, but I will also happily defer to the department's representative here today who might better assist the

committee as you consider this bill.

Good afternoon, Senator Bailey, Representative Mathieson, and Members of the Committee. My
name is Penny Vaillancourt, Deputy Commissioner of the Department of Professional and Financial
Regulation and I am here on behalf of the Office of Professional and Occupational Regulation ("OPOR") testifying in support of LD 448.

The Board of Dental Practice ("the Board") is a professional licensing board within OPOR, which is
an umbrella agency supporting 38 licensing boards and programs. The Board's sole purpose is to protect the public health and welfare of Maine citizens, and it accomplishes this mission by ensuring that the public is served by competent and honest dental professionals through its licensure process, conducting investigations into allegations of unprofessional conduct or incompetent practice, and
imposing sanctions when deemed appropriate.

This bill was submitted at the request of the department once it became known that the statutory
language governing fee caps and the authority to adopt rules setting fee amounts were inadvertently
repealed when the Board joined OPOR as part of the biennial budget last session (PL 2023, c. 17).
The proposed fee caps identified in this bill reflect the fee cap levels that were in place prior to their
repeal. In addition, the bill authorizes the Director of OPOR to set fees amounts necessary to support
the Board's operational needs consistent with the fee rulemaking authority as found in 10 M.R.S.
�8003 sub-�2-A(D).

The fee cap levels identified in this bill can best be summarized by stating that the fee amounts cannot exceed: $200 for dental hygiene licensure; $1000 for dentist licensure and sedation permits; and $550 for any other purpose. Attached is the current fee rule identifying the various licensure categories and
associated fees.

Thank you for the opportunity to comment. I would be happy to answer any questions now or at
work session.

DEPARTMENT OF PROFESSIONAL AND FINANCIAL REGULATION MAINE BOARD OF DENTAL PRACTICE ESTABLISHMENT OF FEES

Summary: This chapter establishes fees for licenses and registrations issued by the Board of Dental
Practice, as well as related fees.

I.

ESTABLISHIVIENT OF FEES; EFFECTIVE DATES

The board shall charge the license and other fees indicated in Section III below. For initial licenses, and for applications and examinations, the fees set out below shall become effective upon the effective date of this chapter. For renewal licenses, the fees set out below shall become effective with the first renewal cycle occurring on or after the effective date of this chapter.

II.

REFUNDS

If an applicant applies for a license or registration listed for which a separate application fee is charged, the license fee will be refunded if the license is denied. All other fees listed in Section HI are
nonrefundable.

The following fees shall be charged for the licenses, registrations and other services listed in subsections 1--- 14 below. For any given license or registration, the designated fee shall apply to both initial issuance and renewal unless otherwise indicated. The term of a license or registration ends on the uniform expiration or renewal date established for that license or registration by law.
